item.title: Top Ed-Tech Tools I've Tried This Year — Honest Reviews for Educators
item.description:
Every year the ed-tech landscape expands. New platforms launch with bold promises, veteran tools ship major updates, and somewhere in the middle of it all, teachers are expected to figure out what’s actually worth their time. This post is my honest attempt to help with that.

I’ve spent the past twelve months genuinely using — not just demoing — the tools below in educational contexts. Here’s what I found.

1. Canva for Education — ★★★★☆

What it promises: A visual design platform that makes creating classroom materials, student presentations, and educational graphics accessible to everyone.

item.title: Why Most Ed-Tech Fails Teachers (And What the Good Stuff Gets Right)
item.description:
There’s a running joke among educators: every September brings a new tool that’s going to change everything, and every June those same tools are forgotten. Having watched this cycle repeat for years, I’ve started to notice the patterns that separate ed-tech that sticks from ed-tech that doesn’t.

The Problem Isn’t the Technology

The tools themselves are rarely the issue. The problem is almost always a mismatch between what a tool was designed to do and the real conditions of a classroom. Ed-tech built by people who haven’t spent time in classrooms tends to optimise for demos, not for daily use.

item.title: What I Learned Building an Interactive Learning Activity from Scratch
item.description:
Last year I set out to build an interactive learning activity from scratch — no template, no pre-existing framework, just a problem I wanted to solve and a blank page. What followed was one of the most instructive experiences I’ve had as both a designer and an educator.

Starting with the Problem, Not the Solution

The temptation when building something new is to start with the format. I wanted to resist that. Instead, I spent the first two weeks just observing — watching where students lost focus, where instructions caused confusion, and where engagement was highest.
